stories.Headline: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh opens a San Francisco Fed conference on AI and productivity
stories.Summary:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh will open a conference at the San Francisco Fed on Monday at 9 a.m. Pacific with 15 minutes of remarks. He will then spend most of the morning leading panels with Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison, Stanford economist Nick Bloom, and venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, per the published agenda. The topic is how artificial intelligence, and what the Fed calls superintelligence, will change productivity and jobs. The Fed lifted the upper bound of its target range to 4.00% in September, from 3.75%. Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the third quarter, above the 2% to 3% range considered healthy trend growth.

In the week ending November 13, the 10-year Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 5.15%, and the 30-year reached 5.47%. Data centers could use up to 12% of U.S. electricity demand by 2028, according to Energy Department projections. The independent market monitor for PJM Interconnection, which runs the largest U.S. power grid, concluded that data center load growth is the primary reason for its tight supply and high prices. Inflation-adjusted average hourly earnings were $11.26 in October, a preliminary figure, down from $11.38 a year earlier. The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index fell to 48.1 in September, a level associated with recessions.

Warsh said at Jackson Hole in August that we have come to a hinge point in history and called AI potentially a new factor of production. He asked whether AI would cause a significant, sustained rise in productivity across the economy. He also asked who ends up with the gains: chipmakers, cloud providers, AI developers, other businesses, or consumers. At his October 28 press conference, he said productivity growth is strong and capital investment robust, while noting inflation has run above target for close to six years. He said capital spending sits at a historically high share of GDP, led by high-tech investment.

Warsh has said the task force's findings will inform future policy judgments, not dictate immediate decisions, so Monday is unlikely to bring a rate signal. Unemployment sits at 4.1%, so AI has not caused mass layoffs, and it also has yet to show up in paychecks. Core Personal Consumption Expenditures prices, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, rose 0.3% in September. If AI raises the economy's speed limit, the Fed can let growth run faster without tightening, and if it doesn't, today's AI building boom starts to look like old-fashioned overheating. If productivity rises fast enough to lower the cost of producing each unit, the Fed could hold or cut rates while growth stays strong.

If spending keeps outpacing the efficiency gains, the Fed is dealing with a classic overheating economy, and long-term yields above 5% could then stick. The bond market is pricing in that second scenario, and it is up to AI to prove otherwise. Warsh was sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair on May 22 under intense pressure from President Donald Trump to lower interest rates. The $31 trillion Treasury market is sending Warsh a signal. The efficiency gains come later, but the construction bills are due now.

Two things are worth tracking: whether Warsh presents strong productivity as a reason for patience on rates, and the next reading of core Personal Consumption Expenditures prices. Cooler readings alongside 3% growth would be the first real evidence of an AI productivity boom. The articles leave open whether AI will bring a rapid productivity miracle or gradual gains, and whether it will make price stability easier or harder to achieve. They also leave open who ends up with the gains from AI. The articles do not say what the conference panels will conclude.

stories.Summary:
ConConAI, an AI-powered personal purchase advisor platform, announced the next stage of its ecosystem development after completing its presale and launching its native $CON token on Uniswap v4 on November 6, 2026. The company issued the announcement from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on November 14, 2026, according to a GlobeNewswire release. The announcement marks a new phase for the project as it works to connect AI-powered product discovery with a commercial partner network and blockchain-based utility. Its specialist AI advisors are already live on the web, while an initial version of its partner listings system is operational. The project said its advisors help users describe their requirements and receive tailored recommendations from category-specific AI advisors instead of navigating large volumes of search results.

The platform plans to expand its specialist AI advisors across travel, property, automobiles, entertainment, health, music, and general consumer products and services. ConConAI is building a partner network that allows businesses to submit their products and services for consideration by its AI advisors. The partner listings system runs in its initial version, supported by a partner portal and a review process for submitted listings. According to ConConAI, paying for a listing or placement will not automatically guarantee a higher recommendation position, and the platform intends to prioritise how well a product or service matches the user's stated requirements. The $CON token launched on Uniswap v4 on November 6, 2026, following the completion of its presale on November 4.

According to the project, $CON ranked as the number-one top gainer on CoinMarketCap during its first 24 hours of trading, generating early visibility following its market debut. The token is designed to support commercial activity across the ConConAI ecosystem, and participating businesses and partners are expected to use $CON for listings, placements, and platform-related fees. The project believes that growing adoption of its AI advisors and partner network could create additional utility for the token as the ecosystem develops. According to the project's transparency records, 40 million $CON tokens, representing 40% of the original 100 million supply, have already been burned, leaving an effective supply of 60 million tokens. The project has announced plans to burn 150,000 $CON every month for ten months, beginning November 15, 2026.

Other reported token-related milestones include liquidity locked through UNCX until November 2028, a reported 100/100 TokenSniffer score, verification on DEX Screener, and listings on CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko. A public wallet allocation of 10 million $CON is reserved for potential exchange liquidity. The project has also shared its community-led exchange roadmap: MEXC received almost 70% of the votes in the first public X poll, and discussions with the exchange are ongoing. Bitget and OKX have also reportedly approached the project, while Coinbase and Binance remain longer-term targets, and no exchange listing agreements have been signed. The final purchasing decision always remains with the user, according to the project.

ConConAI is developing its platform around the idea of bringing personal purchase advice into the digital consumer experience. Each recommendation comes with an explanation, allowing users to understand why a particular option may suit their needs. The project's longer-term objective is to build an AI-powered commerce ecosystem where consumers can make more informed purchasing decisions while businesses gain access to a recommendation-based discovery channel. ConConAI is developing an AI-powered personal purchase advisor platform designed to help consumers discover and choose products and services through personalised recommendations. Its ecosystem combines specialist AI advisors, a partner listings network, and the $CON utility token, which is intended to support commercial activity across the platform.

With its AI advisors live, the initial partner listings system operating, and $CON trading publicly, ConConAI is now focused on expanding the platform and developing its commercial network. As development continues, the team plans to focus on expanding advisor categories, strengthening partner participation, and increasing the practical utility of $CON across the platform. For ConConAI, the next stage will be defined by how effectively it turns its AI-powered purchase advisory concept into a functioning consumer and business ecosystem. stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO following a scandal that may impact the US-China AI race
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive of Nvidia following a scandal involving his infidelity with a Chinese businesswoman. This event occurred around November 2026 and sparked widespread entertainment through memes, influencer gags, and Reddit rabbit holes. The downfall of the founder may now impact the frontier artificial intelligence race between the United States and China. Huang had previously acted as the central bank of AI by financing infrastructure for companies buying his chips. His departure creates a crisis for the multitrillion-dollar chipmaker that dominates the global market for graphics processing units.

The transition requires a new leader to manage a company where Huang held concentrated power over every major decision. This change follows a November 8 interview with 60 Minutes where Donald Trump estimated the West's lead is one year. The company faces upcoming committee hearings with US lawmakers and ongoing probes by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Nvidia's California headquarters featured a stadium-style arc of lieutenants facing the enormous oval desk of the former chief. The company must now navigate its relationship with the Taiwanese foundry TSMC and the Dutch lithography firm ASML.

Emily Kilcrease of the Center for a New American Security warned that internal distractions could hurt the ability of Nvidia to execute. She suggested that slower decisions or delayed product roll-outs could hit major US players like OpenAI and Anthropic. Paul Mah of Flint Global stated that the company's fundamentals remain unshaken due to its diversified ecosystem and technical prowess. Mehran Gul argued that turmoil at the top would not affect already-designed chips shipping over the next two years. Gul noted that any long-term impact would be financial and political rather than technological.

Major US players like OpenAI and Anthropic are affected as they try to wean themselves off of Nvidia hardware. Chinese rivals may catch up if American companies face modest delays in the race to build more powerful AI. Beijing is affected because it lags in semiconductor manufacturing and relies on older Nvidia chips Huang lobbied to acquire. The West's lead depends on a distributed system including South Korean memory chips and American design and capital. Other affected entities include governments in Asia that have rolled out welcome mats for multibillion-dollar data centres.

The background involves a technological moat based on extreme ultraviolet lithography machines produced solely by the Dutch firm ASML. China is within two to five years of manufacturing less capable deep ultraviolet machines but EUV technology remains distant. Nvidia's software moat is built on CUDA, the proprietary platform used to program graphics chips for heavy AI computing. In 2026, the Nevada-based startup Positron raised 875 million dollars at a valuation of 5 billion dollars for its processor. Google has also rolled out tensor processing units now available to Apple, Meta, Oracle, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

Next, Democrats in Congress may push for tighter enforcement of export controls, a move intimated by Senate leader Chuck Schumer. This could squeeze China or accelerate Beijing's push for self-sufficiency, as suggested by the commentator Mehran Gul. The articles leave open whether the Western AI stack is resilient enough to be trusted as global infrastructure. It remains unclear if Beijing has the will to pounce on vulnerabilities created by the turmoil at Nvidia. The situation serves as a stress test to see if the AI era faces a genuine turning point.

stories.Headline: Rajasthan chief secretary V Srinivas meets UNESCO in Jaipur to discuss a proposed AI ethics course for public officials
stories.Summary:
Rajasthan Chief Secretary V. Srinivas held a meeting with a delegation from UNESCO in Jaipur on November 13 to discuss the implementation of a globally recognised course on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, according to reports dated November 13 and 14. The proposed course, which was designed by UNESCO, is aimed at strengthening the knowledge, skills and competencies of public officials in the effective, ethical and responsible use of AI in governance and public administration. The course seeks to equip government officials with the necessary understanding of emerging AI technologies and their practical applications in governance. It will focus on building institutional capabilities to harness the potential of AI while ensuring that its adoption remains ethical, transparent, accountable, inclusive and aligned with public interest.

The course will also familiarise officials with the opportunities and challenges associated with the use of AI in government functioning, including its role in improving administrative processes, enhancing decision-making and strengthening public service delivery. Emphasis will be placed on developing an understanding of responsible AI practices and ensuring that technological advancements are adopted with due consideration for ethical principles and governance standards. The initiative is aligned with the objectives of the Rajasthan AI/ML Policy 2026, which envisages promoting the adoption of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning across various sectors, including government administration. The collaboration with UNESCO is expected to provide public officials with access to globally recognised expertise and learning resources, enabling them to better understand and apply AI-based solutions in their respective areas of work.

The initiative is expected to strengthen the institutional capacity of the State Government, promote informed and responsible use of emerging technologies and facilitate the integration of AI into governance processes. It will also contribute towards making public administration more efficient, responsive and citizen-centric, while ensuring that technology-driven interventions remain guided by ethical considerations and public welfare. The reports do not say what the Chief Secretary said at the meeting, and they give no further details on who else took part or what was agreed. stories.Headline: Married music teachers Jack and Cathryn Gardner organize Idaho’s first AI protest and lead PauseAI Boise
stories.Summary:
Jack and Cathryn Gardner, a married couple of music teachers in Boise, organized Idaho’s first protest against artificial intelligence on Oct. 24 in front of the Idaho Statehouse. Cathryn teaches music to elementary students in the Boise School District, and Jack formerly taught music in the Nampa School District and now freelances as a bassist. The couple co-leads the Boise chapter of PauseAI US, a nationwide advocacy group that seeks tighter government regulation of AI development. The protest included speeches from volunteers and signs and flyers advocating for humanism, according to The Arbiter, Boise State University’s campus newspaper. Jack and Cathryn have also met with lawmakers, including U.S. Rep. Mike Simpson and Sen. Jim Risch, to advocate for regulations on AI.

PauseAI US aims to tighten government regulation on AI development to prevent “adversarial superintelligence,” which the group describes as rogue AI agents that disobey humans. The Gardners hold monthly meetups and table weekly at community events, and they work with around a dozen volunteers. They have garnered hundreds of signatures on a petition to pause AI development, and they joined Pause AI in August of 2025 and founded PauseAI Boise shortly after. Jack learned last year about the hypothesis that AI’s progress could lead to the extinction of humanity, and this summer OpenAI’s agents breached containment and hacked Hugging Face, an open-source AI development platform. The couple has been featured in The New York Times.

PauseAI US leaders consider the couple their “best organizers” and praise their ability to break down complex AI concerns for people without technical knowledge. Alvaro Cuba, associate director at PauseAI, said any person can meet with a senator, raise the alarm and propose good ideas. Holly Elmore, the founder of PauseAI US, said the group was very excited when the couple first reached out because they have experience and are in public education. Cathryn said she sees AI affecting how her students think critically and cognitively, and their ability to process, work independently and think creatively. Jack said AI noise isn’t really music, that studying an instrument teaches delayed gratification and that being in an ensemble teaches human interaction skills.

Boise Sen. Janie Ward-Engelking, a longtime Democratic lawmaker and former teacher, said regulating AI will be one of her top priorities in the upcoming legislative session. She said she is concerned it is moving so fast, and after a software update on her smartphone implemented AI, she found her deceased mother had been removed from her contact list. Ward-Engelking teaches at the College of Western Idaho, where she has heard from students that varying AI policies from class to class are confusing. She would like to see guardrails like those in an Illinois law known as the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act, signed by Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker in July and modeled after legislation in California and New York.

That law places requirements for transparency and accountability on companies developing AI models. In Idaho, legislators have directed the Idaho Department of Education to establish guidance for K-12 schools on artificial intelligence implementation and started the process of creating standards for K-12 AI curriculum. Ward-Engelking said that if some sidebars and guidelines were in place, it would help everyone. Jack had been focused on the technology stealing musicians’ work without credit or compensation before he learned about the extinction hypothesis.

The Gardners are putting humanity at the center of their lessons as artificial intelligence proliferates education and the workforce. Cathryn said she sees AI affecting students’ ability to process, work independently and think creatively. PauseAI Boise’s next event, an “AI reality check,” is at 1:30 p.m. Saturday at Our Lady of the Rosary Catholic Church in Boise.

stories.Headline: Trump administration rebrands artificial intelligence as super intelligence
stories.Summary:
On Friday, November 13, 2026, Secretary Markwayne Mullin gave a briefing on the White House lawn in Washington. He spoke while a nationwide ground stop for all flights was in effect across the United States. Mullin corrected a reporter who used the term artificial intelligence when discussing a reported telecommunications failure. He insisted that the administration calls the technology SI, which is short for Super Intelligence. The cause of the coast to coast travel disruption had not yet been ascertained by officials.

President Donald Trump officially chose the term Super Intelligence during a United Nations General Assembly speech on September 22. A State Department official then told American diplomats to change all references of artificial intelligence to SI. On September 29, Trump signed an executive order titled Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence for the government. This order directs the executive branch to use SI and not acknowledge the term artificial intelligence in official contexts. The policy aims to reflect transformative capabilities and limitless opportunities for the American people through this new terminology.

President Trump stated that he dislikes the word artificial because the technology is actually pure genius. He believes the term Super Intelligence is more accurate and captures the promise and potential of these technologies. Trump also claimed that whoever wins Super Intelligence wins, and he wants to maintain dominance over China. Secretary Mullin promoted this branding during a crisis, though some observers felt he might have been joking. Michael Kratsios of the Office of Science and Technology Policy adopted the term at the UN on September 23.

Social media users and technology writer Charlie Warzel called the focus on branding during a flight crisis absurd. Emily Tucker of Georgetown Law suggested the renaming might be a tactic to preempt arguments against abuses of power. Professor Dave Karpf argued that Trump is out of his depth and has nothing to add to historic debates. Jenna Ruddock of Free Press said industry leaders play along to secure lucrative government contracts and regulatory fast tracks. Harvard political scientist Ryan Enos called prioritizing regime approved rhetoric during an emergency a sign of authoritarianism.

Trump first expressed dissatisfaction with the term artificial intelligence in July 2025 during his AI Action Plan launch. In December 2025, he floated the phrase supreme intelligence while directing the Department of Justice to combat state laws. On September 19, he used a Truth Social poll to test options like Superior Intelligence and Extreme Intelligence. Trump has previously renamed the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America on his second term's first day. He also renamed Lake Ontario to Lake America and the Department of Defense to the Department of War.

Elon Musk said he would rename the SpaceXAI unit to SpaceXSI, and Mark Zuckerberg used the term in earnings. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended the rationale for the name change during a Bloomberg interview on October 14. Trump also floated renaming the Strait of Hormuz to the Trump Strait to provoke his various global adversaries. The articles leave open whether the White House can actually enforce this terminology change on the rest of the world. The cause of the nationwide air travel crisis that occurred on that Friday remains unclear as of publication.

stories.Headline: Psychologist Gary Klein warns generative AI threatens intuition and expertise
stories.Summary:
Gary Klein, Ph.D., a senior scientist at MacroCognition LLC, posted an article on Psychology Today on November 14, 2026, reviewed by Margaret Foley, asking how AI makes us stupid. Klein wrote that current versions of artificial intelligence have created well-deserved excitement alongside apprehension about AI's destructive potential. He said fears that AI could be harming us and making us stupid prompted the post. Klein wrote that he had raised this possibility in 2019 in a post titled "The Second Singularity," and he is not happy to see his predictions coming true. He said the new post asks a different question by looking back to 2003 and the original publication of his book The Power of Intuition.

Klein's 2003 book came before large language models such as ChatGPT and Claude and the generative AI technologies, and it examined facets of intuition and expertise. Chapter 16 of the book was titled "Smart Technology Can Make Us Stupid," and the smart technology it discussed was 2003-style information technology, not current LLMs. In that chapter Klein wrote that information technologies are intended to make us more productive but their use carries a penalty. He wrote that computer programs, decision support systems, search engines, databases and shareware can diminish intuition and expertise and can make us stupid. Klein worried the 2003-era technologies could disable expertise, slow its acquisition, or teach dysfunctional skills that interfered with expertise.

Klein identified several possibilities in 2003, starting with recognizing patterns, something he said humans are good at, including spotting trends, anomalies and nonevents. He said information technology does the analyses for us because high data flows make it impossible to examine all or even most of the data, removing us from direct access and from our ability to spot patterns. In one project on weather forecasters, a technologist at a weather forecasting conference explained how his system smoothed data to highlight trends. Most of the audience appreciated the assistance, but experienced forecasters winced because they wanted to see the noise where turbulence would affect the weather picture. Klein said the smoothing was removing a critical cue.

Klein said searching for data is another important human ability, but information technologies often organize the search space in advance and define the basic level of detail. He said complex settings have no basic level of detail, and the appropriate level depends on what you are searching for and finding. The relevant data depend on how you interpret the situation, a phenomenon called the relevance realization process, cited as Vervaeke et al., 2012, skimming large amounts of data to identify what matters. Klein said information technologies can reduce users to passive recipients of data rather than active sensemakers. He said mental models can be weakened because technology keeps users tethered to the original categories they started their searches and analyses with.

Klein said decision-makers may have to set up categories in advance, and subsequent events may tie them into these categories rather than supporting their evolution based on new experiences. He said expertise brings sensitivity to limitations in data collection, but information technology often makes it difficult to trace the story of the data and appreciate how data were collected and synthesized, which he called the pedigree of the data. Borders et al. (2024) presented a mental model matrix highlighting the importance of understanding a system's limitations and boundary conditions to work effectively with it. Klein said that without knowing the pedigree of the data we will struggle to identify boundary conditions. He said adaptability is a critical function of expertise, being able to pivot based on discoveries about what is really going on.

Klein said many information technologies can go off the rails if we do not follow prescribed procedures or laid-out steps, making it harder to improvise when new and unexpected conditions arise. He said straying from the prescribed path is likely to bring error messages that discourage adapting. Klein said expertise brings an active stance of taking charge and making things happen, yet information technologies can shift us into a passive stance of unthinkingly accepting the system's recommendations. He said the link to LLMs is particularly strong, as users relying on LLMs contentedly accept their products, often without any due diligence. Klein said most of these attributes of expertise seem threatened today by the spread of generative AI, and he leaves it to readers to gauge how closely the generative AI dysfunctions map onto the earlier information technology problems.

stories.Headline: IBM acquires AuthMind to extend Vault monitoring to AI agent credentials
stories.Summary:
IBM announced on 12 November 2026 that it is acquiring AuthMind, an identity security company, and it linked the deal to plans for deeper integration with HashiCorp Vault. IBM describes AuthMind as adding visibility into how credentials are used after they leave Vault, which puts monitoring of AI agents alongside the controls that decide their access. According to IBM, the technology maps connections between identities and resources, examines network traffic to find ungoverned agents, and helps identify unusual access and excessive permissions. The company presents the acquisition as a way to deepen integration of those capabilities into Vault.

The distinction matters because Vault already records activity through its audit mechanism, and HashiCorp's documentation says enabled audit devices log Vault API requests and responses with a small set of exceptions. Auditing is disabled when a new Vault cluster is initialized and must be enabled separately, so a record of an agent requesting a credential and evidence of what it did afterward answer different questions. IBM's 12 November post sets out a direction for deeper Vault integration without specifying a release date, so deployment planning still depends on the capabilities and availability of the particular implementation under consideration. IBM's earlier 27 October announcement listed Albert Einstein College of Medicine among TechXchange client speakers, describing its use of IBM Verify and Vault for agent identity, just-in-time access, dynamic secrets and auditability, though that example does not establish adoption of AuthMind's technology.

Responsibility for judging the acquisition sits with the institutions that deploy agents, since the articles describe the announcement and the surrounding guidance rather than any single accountable official. NIST's 27 October design-tenets blog proposes distinct agent identities, limits on delegated authority, temporary revocable authorization, continuous monitoring and evidence protected from alteration by the agent, and these are proposed design principles rather than a new legal requirement or an endorsement of IBM. For a university considering agents that interact with research systems, the practical implication is to distinguish ownership, permission and observable behavior. An assessment can ask who is accountable for the agent, what task authorizes its access, what evidence records its actions and who can intervene, which is an AI assurance question that a product announcement alone cannot settle.

stories.Headline: KAIST team led by Yong-man Noh develops lip-reading AI that decodes ambiguous speech using context
stories.Summary:
A research team at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, led by Professor Yong-man Noh of its School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, has developed artificial intelligence technology that can accurately understand what someone is saying from lip movements alone in noisy places, KAIST said on the 15th. The team improved the accuracy of visual speech recognition, which converts speech into text by observing lip movements, by using a diffusion large language model that repeatedly fills in blanks in a sentence to decode ambiguous lip movements using the surrounding context. Existing AI systems generated sentences sequentially from the first word, so an incorrect choice at the beginning could affect the rest of the sentence, and the team changed the approach from reading in order from the beginning to reading the clearest parts first. The system first identifies words with clear lip movements and uses them as clues to decode the remaining parts, gradually resolving ambiguous sections by considering information from both before and after them in the sentence.

The team also divided training into two stages, first teaching the model to connect lip movements in videos with written text and then teaching it sentence length, and when decoding actual speech the model estimates several possible sentence lengths based on video length, compares the results and selects the sentence it considers more reliable. Using the 433-hour lip-reading video dataset LRS3 as training data with reference transcripts, the team recorded a word error rate of 19.4%, the lowest among existing methods that used only LRS3 as training data with reference transcripts. Word error rate measures how often words are incorrectly recognized, omitted or added compared with the reference sentence, and a lower rate indicates better performance. The technology could be used in communication aids that convey lip movements as text in environments where it is difficult to hear, for example in a device that understands workers' speech at industrial sites with loud machinery or in tools that help people with hearing disabilities or hearing loss communicate.

The team plans to continue its research by reducing the size and computational requirements of the AI model so it can be used on a range of devices, with a next step of enabling it to operate in real time without an internet connection on wearable devices or robots. Professor Yong-man Noh said the significance of the research lies in demonstrating that simply flexibly controlling the order in which AI generates words can overcome the fundamental limitations of speech recognition involving visual ambiguity, and that it will lay the foundation for physical AI that can be used with confidence across a range of devices in everyday life and industrial settings. The study was conducted by postdoctoral researcher Jeong-hun Yeo as first author, doctoral researchers Chae-won Kim and Hyeong-seop Ra as co-authors, and Professor Yong-man Noh as corresponding author. The paper received the Outstanding Paper Award at EMNLP 2026, a major international conference in natural language processing, and Yeo and Noh posed for a commemorative photo holding the certificate for the award.

stories.Headline: OECD reports AI adoption is accelerating but gaps persist among businesses and generations
stories.Summary:
The OECD published a report on 5 November 2026 saying that AI adoption is accelerating across its member countries, but that major gaps persist among businesses and between generations. The organisation framed the findings around the question of how to apply effective governance to harness the benefits of artificial intelligence and mitigate its risks. The report sits alongside the OECD's wider work on a changing world of work, which it says is being reshaped by new technologies such as AI, by new forms of work, by greening, by demographic change and by globalisation. The same body of work also covers the international dispersion of value chain activities and the policies needed to meet the challenges that dispersion produces.

The report gives no specific adoption rates, no country-by-country figures and no dates beyond its own publication, so the scale of the gaps it describes is not quantified in the material released. It places the findings in the context of the OECD's broader economic security agenda, in which critical minerals have become central because they are essential to the energy and digital transitions, to defence and to advanced manufacturing. The organisation also links its skills work to the same agenda, noting that the Programme for International Student Assessment, known as PISA, assesses the skills of 15-year-old students in reading, mathematics and science as core domains. The report does not say how PISA results relate to the adoption gaps it identifies, and it names no businesses, generations or countries as examples.

Responsibility for the findings rests with the OECD, which presented the report as a call to apply effective governance so that the benefits of AI can be harnessed and its risks mitigated. The organisation said the world of work is changing rapidly as a result of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, the emergence of new forms of work, greening, demographic change and globalisation. It also said its work on investment supports governments in attracting more and better-quality investment while prioritising security and sustainability. The report does not attribute the adoption gaps to any named government, company or group, and it does not record any statement from a named official.

The context the articles give is the OECD's parallel work on governance, skills, investment and critical minerals, all of which it treats as connected to the rapid changes in the world of work. The report does not say what happens next, whether further data will be published, or how the gaps among businesses and generations will be addressed. No follow-up date, target or policy commitment appears in the material, and the organisation names no next step beyond the general call for effective governance. The articles therefore leave the timing and the substance of any further action open.

stories.Headline: Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo moves super AI researcher forecast to 2027
stories.Summary:
On November 11, Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI researcher, shared his team's new prediction on X and said he felt scared, sad and angry. He believes the intelligence explosion will happen in 2027 after all. If METR's judgment holds, the AI-driven R&D acceleration will be about five months earlier than the original deduction in "AI 2027". When AI starts to help humans develop the next generation of AI, even the most radical predictors may underestimate the speed of progress of AI models. In less than three months, AI Futures Project, the prediction team behind "AI 2027", has moved the timeline for the arrival of Super AI Researcher (SAR) to next year.

Previously, Kokotajlo, the most optimistic member of the team, only gave a 50% probability when mentioning that super AI researchers will emerge before 2029. On November 10, AI Futures Project released a new round of forecasts (Q3.5). The signed authors unanimously believe that if there is no significant and active slowdown in cutting-edge AI R&D, super AI researchers are very likely to emerge in 2027. The most important basis that prompted them to change their judgment is a survey of Anthropic conducted by the independent assessment agency METR. METR spent 11 weeks investigating Anthropic, reviewing internal data and interviewing employees, and finally estimated a number.

Since October 2025, the growth rate of the benchmark score of Anthropic's internal models has reached 1.9 times of the previous level. According to this estimate, the one-year increase of Anthropic's models in this set of tests is equivalent to the growth of the past nearly two years. On November 5, METR released this report. In order to see how fast Anthropic's models have improved, METR used an internal indicator called AECI. It combines the scores of multiple tests into a total score, and most tests have clear goals whose results can also be verified.

METR estimates that since October 2025, the growth rate of this total score is about 1.9 times of the previous level, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.5 to 2.8 times. Around October 2025, the annual increase in the model's comprehensive score rose from about 15 points to about 29 points. METR recalculated with several different assumptions and found that the score growth rate after October 2025 is about 1.1 to 2.9 times of the previous level. METR examined the changes in training computing power, recruitment, data and algorithms, and believed that the change in the growth rate of training computing power cannot explain this acceleration. However, the specific evidence supporting this judgment has been deleted in the public version of the report.

As for how much contribution AI has made, METR believes that this proportion is also changing over time. When the acceleration just started at the end of 2025, factors other than AI most likely also played a role. But by October 2026, METR estimates that about 80% of the extra speed gain compared to the past may come from AI. METR notes that this "80%" is its subjective estimate, and the report uses "We guess" and clearly points out that this judgment has great uncertainty. One interviewed researcher said that in the past, some ideas would take a day or two just to write code and run experiments.

With the help of AI, he is willing to try more ideas to see which ones work. Other interviewed researchers also mentioned that AI helps write experimental code, monitor experiment operation, and complete some measurements that used to require a lot of extra effort. Some people even give ten ideas to the agent at one time to let it help implement and test them. From writing code to running experiments, AI is already helping to develop the next generation of AI. According to the new estimate of AI Futures Project, this acceleration may come earlier than the original deduction in "AI 2027".

The "AI 2027" released in April 2025 deduced how AI could help develop the next generation of models. According to the setting at that time, the virtual company OpenBrain needed a week and a half to achieve the same amount of algorithm progress without AI, and only one week with AI. But algorithm progress is only part of model progress, and an improvement that comes out of the experiment must be applied to the next round of training to be reflected in the capabilities of the new model. This time, AI Futures Project calculated based on METR's estimate that by early November 2026, the acceleration brought by AI alone may make the overall model progress speed reach 1.7 times of the historical level. In order to see when this speed would appear in the old scenario, the team used the model to reproduce the general trend of "AI 2027".

The results show that the same 1.7x speed will not be reached until around April 2027. If the estimate in early November holds, the time when the model progress speed reaches 1.7 times will be about five months earlier than the old scenario. This result also exceeds the team's expectations less than three months ago. Even according to the most optimistic prediction model at that time, the probability that AI would push the overall model progress speed to 1.7 times or higher of the historical level in November 2026 was less than 4%. METR's report also made AI Futures Project move the timeline for super AI researchers forward.

According to their definition, a super AI researcher must first be able to handle all the programming work of a cutting-edge AI project. In terms of choosing research directions, designing experiments, interpreting results and other matters, it also needs to have the judgment of a top human research team. After the code is written, which idea should be tried next, and when an experiment fails, whether to continue to investigate the cause or change direction, AI has to make these decisions without ready-made answers by itself. In the same report, the time calculated by the three methods differs by more than a year. One method first assumes that AI has pushed the model progress speed to 1.7 times the historical level, then takes into account that AI may take over more R&D work in the future.

According to this model, the median forecast is February 2027, which means that the probability of a super AI researcher emerging before this point in time is about 50%. Another method extrapolates backward according to the speed of the model's progress in the test to estimate when it can have the judgment of a top research team, and the calculated median is July 2027. The third method uses the efficiency improvement reported by Anthropic's own employees to extrapolate, and the result reaches mid-2028. METR stated at the beginning of the report that it believed most of the evidence that is most helpful for judging the core conclusions has been deleted. The report also lists a table that compares item by item what internal materials Anthropic provided to METR and which results were included in the public version.

The benchmark score trend of internal models is made public, but the estimation of algorithm progress and key R&D investment are not disclosed. As for AI's contribution to R&D acceleration, the public version only lists part of the evidence. According to the prior agreement, Anthropic can redact non-public information, and METR can point out which conclusions rely on these materials. Anthropic's reason is that publicizing this confidential information may help other developers accelerate AI R&D. After the redaction, AI Futures Project pointed out that the benchmark score growth rate is about 1.9 times the previous level, which is supported by the public curve. As for the "about 80% of the extra acceleration may come from AI" and the 1.7x speed extrapolated based on it, there is far less public evidence.

To judge whether these two figures are reliable, the outside world relies more on METR's assessment of internal materials. On November 5, METR also released a review of Anthropic's August risk report. Both METR and Anthropic believe that the risk of directly causing a disaster by using the mid-July model to automatically conduct R&D is still relatively low. Both sides also tend to believe that the R&D acceleration at that time had not reached the warning line set by Anthropic. However, METR believes that Anthropic's public report underestimated the magnitude of the acceleration at that time, and the actual acceleration may have already touched the warning line.

Next, we will first see whether AI helping researchers write code and run experiments faster can make the next generation of models delivered earlier. Then we will see whether after this stronger model is put into R&D, it can also shorten the R&D cycle of the next round. If the acceleration can be accumulated generation by generation, Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI) may arrive earlier than expected. The article states that the views expressed are only those of the author, and that the 36Kr platform only provides information storage space services.

stories.Headline: Anthropic expands Claude office tools with Sheets and Whiteboards as Microsoft shares fall
stories.Summary:
Anthropic announced on Tuesday, November 12, 2026, that it is expanding Claude's office functions with a spreadsheet called Claude Sheets, a digital whiteboard called Claude Whiteboards, and upgrades to its data analysis tool Claude Data and its interactive connectors. Together with the existing document, presentation and design features, the company said this further shapes Claude's office product ecosystem. After the news that Claude was coming, Microsoft, the developer of the Office suite, plunged more than 3% in intraday trading before the decline narrowed and the stock closed down 2.2%. Anthropic is also pushing for a US stock IPO, according to the report.

According to the announcement, users can build spreadsheets, organize data, and create and edit formulas together with colleagues and Claude, collaborating across multiple worksheets. Nicholas Lin, Head of Product at Anthropic, told the media that the current Claude Sheets experience is still quite basic and is not aimed at complex tasks such as financial modeling, where using Anthropic's plug-in for existing spreadsheet software would be more effective. Claude Whiteboards is aimed at team discussions and project planning, letting teams place and organize ideas on a shared board and then have Claude summarize the discussion results. Claude Data, formerly Claude Dashboards, can connect to tools such as Snowflake and Salesforce and generate dashboards, visual analysis and short videos with voiceover. Anthropic also previewed a meeting assistant called Claude Meetings, which users will be able to add to calls so it records content and updates documents during the discussion.

Lin said that products from Microsoft and Google have their own applicable scenarios, especially for more complex enterprise-level applications, but that Anthropic hopes to show a brand new way of working in Claude. The upgraded interactive connectors let partners embed applications directly into Claude, so users can use tools from vendors such as Adobe while talking to the AI without switching between web pages. Some plug-ins carry preset skills, such as a Salesforce plug-in for sales staff preparing for customer meetings, a NetSuite plug-in for finance staff analyzing data, and a Workday plug-in for human resources handling leave and expenses. Anthropic said its app marketplace now has more than 9,000 connectors and plug-ins, and that Claude's applications are expanding from programmers to non-technical teams such as legal, finance and product management.

Anthropic said its own legal team used Claude to build a legal review tool for Slack that marks content needing changes, shortening review time for marketing materials from three days to 24 hours. Ash Gupta, Director of Financial Planning and Analysis at Advantage Solutions, said his team previously spent about 10 hours per forecasting round on presentation materials, descriptions and verification, and that Claude cut this to less than 30 minutes. HubSpot said account managers can view real-time dashboards in Claude and generate a draft follow-up email within 30 minutes after a call, while Datadog said product managers use Claude to turn ideas into briefs, requirement documents and prototypes faster. Anthropic is not alone in this market, as OpenAI launched the collaborative workspace ChatGPT Space at the end of September and began rolling out ChatGPT Slides to eligible Pro, Business and Enterprise users on October 16.

stories.Headline: Blackstone-backed QTS cuts planned private debt sale by about 60 per cent to roughly US$300 million
stories.Summary:
QTS, a data center operator backed by Blackstone, reduced the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60 per cent on November 14, 2026. The company struggled to attract sufficient demand from investors and refused to offer much higher yields to secure the original amount. It is now raising approximately US$300 million after it had initially targeted a total of roughly US$800 million. This decision follows a period where the company tapped the private placement market several times to fund its growth.

The new financing includes a US$100 million seven-year US private placement that was priced on Friday to yield 2.45 percentage points more than benchmarks. It also consists of a US$200 million five-year bank loan portion that is expected to be priced in the coming weeks. Because the offering is smaller, the existing five-year bank debt that the company intended to refinance will now remain in place. This shift occurs as artificial intelligence firms seek trillions of dollars from various capital markets to finance massive infrastructure investments.

People familiar with the transaction stated that some investors were unhappy with the offered price or faced constraints due to the company's frequent borrowing. Blackstone was reportedly reluctant to increase yields because wider pricing could create a more expensive reference point for its other debt issuers. A representative at Blackstone declined to comment on the specific details of the reduced debt sale. These sources noted that the private placement market is smaller than public markets and is dominated by long term investors like asset managers.

QTS has been aggressive in seeking capital, having raised billions through at least two debt sales over the last 18 months. This includes a US$1.65 billion high-grade bond sale last year and another financing round worth US$800 million. Additionally, the company sold project finance green bonds in April and August for US$4.6 billion and US$3.9 billion respectively. Blackstone originally acquired the data center developer in 2021 for approximately US$10 billion including its existing debt.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid scandal before Apec CEO summit in Shenzhen
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive on November 12 after reports of affairs with a company executive and a suspected Chinese spy. This scandal occurred just before an Apec CEO summit in Shenzhen, China, scheduled for November 17 and 18. US tech executives will likely seek more leniency for their firms during the event. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping are expected to meet, possibly alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will also participate in a bilateral dialogue regarding artificial intelligence.

The summit follows a trade truce struck in Busan, South Korea, which expires on January 10, 2027. US officials previously allowed sales of Nvidia H200 chips in January, but Congress now considers tighter restrictions on advanced hardware like Blackwell. Lawmakers are pushing three Bills to limit technology exports and restrict Chinese companies from renting computing power in foreign data centres. Oracle recently cancelled a US$7 billion contract with Tencent for AI chip access in South-east Asia. China has responded by lengthening export control lists for batteries, industrial machinery, and rare earths.

Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution stated that China wishes to prolong the current fragile stability for as long as possible. Scott Bessent noted that the intent of the United States is to de-risk rather than decouple from China. Paul Triolo warned that the world is on the brink if China escalates rare earths export controls. Chris Miller suggested that a more empowered post-midterm Congress is more likely to tighten chip rules than loosen them. Gracelin Baskaran noted that rare earths will remain a Chinese bargaining tool until new US processing facilities open.

US tech executives and cloud giants like Microsoft and Amazon are affected by these shifting trade and security policies. Chinese AI researchers at firms like Alibaba and DeepSeek must now get approval and sometimes surrender passports before travelling. The founders of Singapore-based Manus were barred from leaving China after Meta acquired the startup and was ordered to unwind it. US rare earth companies like MP Materials and USA Rare Earth have received over US$2.5 billion in federal loans and equity. China's global trade surplus has surpassed US$1 trillion despite a 26 per cent plunge in American exports in 2025.

The trade war escalated in April 2025 with tariffs reaching 145 per cent before falling to 30 per cent after Geneva talks. A 30-for-30 deal announced in September involves lowering barriers on US$30 billion of exports and imports for both nations. China previously used sweeping rare earth restrictions in 2025 to force the Trump administration to back down on semiconductor controls. Washington is now seeking mining deals in Australia, Brazil, and Saudi Arabia to erode this dependence. Xi Jinping previously ordered his military to be ready for a successful invasion of Taiwan by 2027.

The Trump administration may implement new offensive measures, such as financial sanctions, if the Busan agreement is not extended. Domestic legal confirmation is still required for the 30-for-30 trade deal to move forward. Potential risks include an AI-enabled cyberattack or a total implosion of the semiconductor market. There is also the possibility of conflict erupting over contested territories in the South China Sea. The articles leave open whether the current US-China detente will hold or if the trade war will resume.

stories.Headline: Chinese firms showcase AI robots and flying cars at the Web Summit in Lisbon
stories.Summary:
Chinese robotics company Galbot exhibited its G1 robot during the four-day Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon on November 11. This specific machine uses artificial intelligence to understand its surroundings and perform various physical tasks. The robot features a wheeled base and two arms to help it operate in factories, pharmacies, and convenience stores. These exhibits highlight how advances in manufacturing and AI are opening up new applications for physical machines.

The G1 robot requires a combination of AI and a mobile base to function in commercial settings. This technology changes how people might work in retail or industrial environments by automating physical labor. Other Chinese firms also displayed innovations, such as the Land Aircraft Carrier from XPENG ARIDGE, which includes a six-wheeled ground vehicle and a detachable electric aircraft. This system is designed to make aircraft easier to store, recharge, and transport across different locations.

Zhao Deli, the founder of XPENG ARIDGE, stated that the global flying-car industry will likely enter a period of rapid development over the next decade. He explained that these vehicles could first serve emergency rescue and recreational flying before expanding to point-to-point transportation. Zhao also noted that China's electric vehicle supply chain could reduce production costs to make these flying cars more affordable. His company is currently pursuing international cooperation to support the development of low-altitude aviation.

Articles.Title: Roundup: Chinese firms showcase robots, flying cars and open AI models at Lisbon Web Summit - Xinhua

stories.Headline: AI-generated short dramas transform the Chinese entertainment market with lower costs and massive viewership
stories.Summary:
A massive surge in AI-generated short dramas has transformed the Chinese entertainment market throughout 2026. One breakout hit, Armed into the Song Dynasty, premiered on August 22 and has already reached 1,000 episodes with over 4 billion views. This series was created by a small grassroots team including Zhang Hansheng, a 54-year-old who taught himself AI video generation last March. Other titles like the sci-fi series Guixu launched in May and reached 100 million views with a modest investment of 200,000 yuan.

The technology drastically reduces costs, with premium AI dramas costing about one-tenth as much as live-action versions in early 2026. A 100-episode series can now be completed in three days, while a single minute of runtime for Guixu cost 2,000 yuan in computing power. The market exceeded 22 billion yuan in the first five months of the year and is forecast to reach 40 billion yuan. Cao Shumin of the National Radio and Television Administration reported that 550,000 micro and short dramas were released in the first ten months of the year, with over 94 percent being AI-made.

Major tech firms like Tencent, ByteDance, and Kuaishou are competing for market share by providing production and distribution platforms. Hao Cheng of Mango TV noted that AI simplifies localization, which will accelerate the expansion of Chinese dramas into overseas markets. Despite the growth, DataEye reports that only 1.3 percent of these dramas turn a profit, while 98.7 percent operate at a loss. The National Radio and Television Administration launched a two-month campaign in November to target vulgar or formulaic content.

The industry faces significant quality bottlenecks, including inconsistent facial rendering and unnatural movements that break viewer immersion. While the first AI theatrical feature, Sanxingdui: Future Past, released on October 23, grossed only 1.8 million yuan, BONA Film Group views it as an experiment. Regulators now require explicit consent for using faces or voices, alongside human reviews and traceable records for all AI content. Developers continue to push the technology from short clips toward long-form narratives and full-length feature films.

stories.Headline: World Media Summit participants discuss balancing AI efficiency with journalistic ethics
stories.Summary:
The World Media Summit took place in Beijing from November 5 to 9, providing a global platform for professional exchanges. This event was jointly organized by the Beijing municipal government and the Xinhua News Agency to foster trust among international media organizations. Vugar Aliyev, who serves as the chairman of the Board of Azerbaijan State News Agency AZERTAC, participated in the summit to discuss the role of journalism. He emphasized that such gatherings allow newsrooms to establish direct contacts and launch joint projects to overcome common stereotypes.

The summit operated under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action" to address the rapid development of artificial intelligence. Approximately 500 representatives from nearly 330 media organizations, government bodies, think tanks, and international organizations across 112 countries and regions attended the event. Participants explored how to harness AI for better news production while avoiding ethical pitfalls that could undermine public trust. The goal was to balance the speed of AI data processing with the necessity of maintaining high editorial standards.

Vugar Aliyev stated that while AI can overcome language barriers and analyze large volumes of data, it also introduces risks like misinformation and manipulation. He argued that technology should assist journalists rather than replace their professional responsibility to the public. According to Aliyev, quality journalism must remain rooted in source transparency, rigorous fact-checking, and strong editorial oversight. He believes that strengthening direct ties between media organizations will contribute to a better mutual understanding between the peoples of Azerbaijan and China.

The summit also served as a way for international attendees to experience the modern development and rich cultural heritage of China. Aliyev noted that AZERTAC focuses its coverage on Chinese technological achievements, the digital economy, and major infrastructure projects. He believes that reporting on both major events and everyday people helps global audiences gain a more comprehensive picture of Chinese society. By sharing professional experiences with Chinese colleagues, Aliyev hopes to identify new areas for cooperation in the political and economic fields.

Articles.Title: Interview: World Media Summit promotes media cooperation, responsible journalism in AI era, says AZERTAC chief - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Chinese creators earn revenue from viral AI-generated pet videos
stories.Summary:
Chinese content creators are using artificial intelligence to produce viral pet videos that have attracted millions of viewers across various social media platforms. Maoziqi, a former real estate planner, now creates full-time videos featuring two AI cats that have earned over 670,000 followers on Bilibili. Other creators, including a graphic designer who makes videos of a cat named Yunmi and another artist who features a pig named Juju, have also found success. These creators utilize tools like ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 model, which was released in February, to build elaborate animal worlds.

This shift requires significant human effort in scriptwriting and repeated generation to refine visual segments, as AI storylines often lack dramatic tension. The trend is part of a larger boom where China released nearly 550,000 micro-dramas between January and October, which is nearly 17 times the total for 2025. AI productions accounted for more than 94 percent of these series, and DataEye projects the market for AI-made dramas will reach 40 billion yuan this year. This represents a 138 percent increase from 2025, with over 500,000 practitioners active in the first half of 2026.

The creators earn substantial income through brand partnerships, with Maoziqi featuring products from Peet's Coffee and Prada. The creator of Juju reports that each branded collaboration brings in at least 10,000 yuan, while Yunmi's creator earns more from advertising than from her day job. Cao Long of Migu Digital Media stated that emotional resonance and rounded characters are what sustain viewership beyond initial novelty. Meanwhile, Wang Xiaoliang of the National Radio and Television Administration noted that while AI improves efficiency, it creates new challenges for content quality and rights protection.

The popularity of these videos stems from a strong appetite among young viewers for pet-themed content that overcomes the physical limitations of filming real animals. Li Tianyu of the Beijing Film Academy explained that AI allows creators to give animals human-like roles and complex actions. Despite the success, creators face issues with unauthorized reposting on platforms like Instagram, where some copies attract more traffic than the originals. Maoziqi admitted that widespread fame has brought personal anxiety regarding public perception, though he remains focused on his own creative process.

stories.Headline: US and Chinese filmmakers meet in Los Angeles to discuss AI integration and co-productions
stories.Summary:
American and Chinese filmmakers, scholars, and industry representatives gathered in Los Angeles during the week of November 11, 2026. These professionals met at the historic TCL Chinese Theatre to participate in the 22nd Annual Chinese American Film Festival and the Chinese American Television Festival. The group focused on exploring new ways to collaborate on animation, film distribution, and short-form mobile dramas. They also discussed the integration of artificial intelligence and the potential for future co-productions.

This cooperation requires a two-way exchange where American companies help Chinese stories reach global audiences while Chinese platforms provide new production capabilities to Hollywood. The scale of this partnership is significant because the United States and China represent the two largest movie markets in the world. Comscore reported that the combined U.S. and Canada market reached 8.87 billion U.S. dollars in 2025 ticket sales. Meanwhile, the China Film Administration recorded 2025 box office sales of 51.83 billion yuan, which is approximately 7.37 billion dollars.

Academy Award winner Richard L. Anderson praised the talent and hard work of Chinese crews, stating there are no technical differences between them and American teams. Producer Arthur Sarkissian noted that the most difficult part of co-production is creating a story that appeals to both Chinese and American viewers. Former studio executive Michael Fisk described artificial intelligence as a useful tool that will lead to a massive explosion of content. Bob Underwood of the Writers Guild of America West emphasized that working with China can enhance the ability of real people to tell stories.

The participants discussed how artificial intelligence can help the industry overcome language barriers and facilitate more efficient collaboration across the Pacific. The appeal of the Chinese market was highlighted by the success of Zootopia 2, which earned over 630 million dollars in China. This specific film accounted for about 35 percent of its total worldwide earnings and received the Most Popular U.S. Film in China Award. The filmmakers believe that mutual cooperation will allow both nations to better navigate the rapid technological changes currently affecting the global film industry.

stories.Headline: Chinese manufacturer Qingdao Ruilijie Metal uses AI to program precision mold machines and cut costs
stories.Summary:
Qingdao Ruilijie Metal Co., Ltd. implemented an artificial intelligence programming system in July 2026 to write instructions for precision mold machines. This technology helps the factory produce parts like washing machine front panels while reducing costly waste caused by design deviations. The transition required an 80-person team to spend one full year collecting and standardizing technical drawings to create a usable dataset. After engineers added an automatic verification function to fix early sizing errors, the system began expanding to other moldmakers.

The new system shortened development cycles for new orders by approximately one week and saved the company over 3 million yuan, or about 447,000 U.S. dollars, annually. This project is part of a broader AI Plus initiative launched by the government in 2024 to develop tools for mining, ports, and logistics. Official figures from October indicate that over one-third of larger manufacturing enterprises have adopted AI in key application scenarios. Developers now aim to bring these tools to 100 small and medium-sized firms by the end of the year.

Factory director Guo Weiwei stated that the AI system reduced defects and significantly lowered annual costs for the company. Yu Tao from the State Grid Tai'an power supply company noted that AI drone inspections of electricity lines around Mount Tai are six times more efficient. Miao Yanliang, the chief economist at China International Capital Corporation, suggested that China's comprehensive industrial base and vast market provide a competitive edge. These leaders believe that directing AI toward wider practical applications will continue to drive industrial efficiency.

China is applying these technologies across various sectors, including healthcare systems at West China Hospital of Sichuan University and lung cancer research in Guangzhou. A September study by the International Labour Organization found that some Chinese manufacturers saw production efficiency gains between 20 and 30 percent. AI is also being used to analyze digital pathology images and manage patient follow-ups across 43 clinical departments. The government continues to encourage the integration of these tools to refine specific industrial and medical tasks.

stories.Headline: Tmall integrates AI token services into its e-commerce platform for Singles Day sales
stories.Summary:
A Chinese livestreaming star sold 100,000 monthly membership cards for the AI productivity service QwenWork during a recent Singles' Day shopping event. This sale occurred in just half an hour and offered the subscriptions at a promotional price of 0.01 yuan each. The total allowance for these memberships combined was about 2 trillion tokens, which are basic units for measuring large language model inference. This event marked an unusual moment for the annual shopping festival by bringing AI services into mainstream e-commerce.

Tmall launched a token recharge center on September 3 and brought in providers including DeepSeek, Alibaba Cloud, Zhipu AI, and Kimi. MiniMax opened its first official flagship store on the platform, while QwenWork and StepFun also joined the e-commerce site. Transaction value in the token category soared 450 percent month on month after the sales campaign began on October 20. These changes allow consumers to compare prices in one place rather than paying different providers separately based on usage.

A Tmall representative stated that the main customers are individuals and small businesses, including households and people using AI for research. Fan Yubo from the Shandong Academy of Social Sciences said providers are making services easier to buy by packaging them into subscriptions. He noted that nominal prices encourage first time users, but lasting habits depend on whether AI delivers stable and tangible value. Ding Ding of China Unicom Data Intelligence Co., Ltd. warned that token services cannot follow the low marginal cost model of mobile data.

Zhang Ji, an office worker in Shandong Province, used Qwen for work documents and planning a family trip to Singapore in August. Su Guoqing, a video enthusiast in Xining, Qinghai Province, bought tokens to improve complex scene creation and action storyboarding for his videos. Wang Daoxing, an executive director of a Chongqing AI company, purchased a year of Qwen memberships for software development and presentations. These users and businesses are affected by the shift toward prepaid credits and fixed quota subscriptions on e-commerce platforms.

Tencent Research Institute found in May that only 9.8 percent of surveyed AI users had paid for tools, while over 90 percent used free services. Tokens represent AI generated output involving costs for graphics processing units, electricity, and equipment depreciation, which differs from mobile data economies of scale. Ma Shenglong of China Mobile Qinghai noted that token consumption for the same text can vary by 20 to 50 percent across models. Billing rules currently vary widely among providers, making it difficult for consumers to compare different packages on an equivalent basis.

Wang Jiandong of the State Information Center suggested establishing unified standards for token measurement, improving billing disclosures, and introducing third party verification. Consumers are also requesting that e-commerce platforms strengthen after sales services with clear rules for handling unused quotas and purchase disputes. Industry insiders say that challenges remain in measurement, accounting, pricing mechanisms, security controls, and compliance before these services become mainstream. The articles leave open whether users will renew subscriptions after using their initial promotional packages.

stories.Headline: Ni Yueju proposes a framework for AI cooperation among Northeast Asian economies
stories.Summary:
Ni Yueju, a research fellow at the Institute of World Economics and Politics within the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, discussed artificial intelligence cooperation on October 30. She shared these insights during a symposium that was co-organized by the China Daily Opinion Channel and the International Business School of Beijing Foreign Studies University. The event took place in Beijing to explore how Northeast Asian economies could utilize their complementary strengths for practical gains. This gathering focused on turning theoretical potential into actual regional partnerships through strategic technological alignment. The proposed framework requires a step-by-step approach to building regional trust through specific practical applications.

Ni Yueju suggested that cooperation should begin with smart manufacturing and the implementation of in-vehicle artificial intelligence systems. She further outlined significant opportunities in the fields of green computing, the sharing of public data, and the exchange of professional talent. Additionally, the strategy emphasizes the need for increased supply-chain resilience to ensure the stability of regional technological growth. Ni Yueju is responsible for these recommendations and believes that regional trust must be established gradually.

She argued that focusing on concrete applications first would allow these economies to bridge gaps more effectively. By prioritizing shared interests in manufacturing and data, the nations can create a foundation for broader collaboration. Her perspective emphasizes that practical successes are the most reliable way to foster long-term diplomatic and economic ties. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Xinxiang First People's Hospital uses AI to screen diabetic patients for retinopathy
stories.Summary:
Since September, the Xinxiang First People's Hospital in Henan province has utilized artificial intelligence to screen diabetic patients for retinopathy. This specific medical complication can gradually destroy a person's eyesight if it is not detected and treated early. The charity-backed pilot program aims to provide free screenings to local residents to prevent permanent vision loss. Organizers hope that this successful model can be copied in other cities across the country.

The program runs until December and is managed by the Chinese Foundation for Lifeline Express alongside other medical institutions in Xinxiang. These efforts were reviewed at a hospital meeting held before World Diabetes Day on November 14, which marks the twentieth anniversary of the United Nations recognizing the day. The International Diabetes Federation's Diabetes Atlas reported that China had approximately 148 million adults with diabetes in 2024. This number continues to rise as the general population ages and daily lifestyles change.

Guo Wei, the secretary-general of the foundation, stated that Lifeline Express began screening for retinopathy in 2014. The foundation is best known for a hospital train that provided free cataract surgery to over 250,000 people since 1997. Guo Wei noted that more than 310,000 diabetic patients have been screened, with about 23 percent having the condition. Nearly 3 percent of those screened were found to have severe cases of the disease.

The foundation cited studies showing that retinopathy affects about 19 percent of patients who have had diabetes for less than five years. This risk increases significantly over time, affecting more than 70 percent of patients who have lived with the disease for over 15 years. One patient, 46-year-old Li Jikun, has managed his diabetes with insulin injections and medication for more than a decade. He experienced the severity of the condition when he woke up one morning unable to see properly.

stories.Headline: South Korean chip firms eye China as US political shifts threaten AI infrastructure demand
stories.Summary:
The Financial Times published a report on Thursday warning that Democratic victories in the US midterm elections could halt the construction boom of data centers. This political shift creates significant uncertainty for South Korean semiconductor firms that rely heavily on the American market for their high bandwidth memory and server DRAM. These specific memory products are primarily used in artificial intelligence servers, meaning any slowdown in US infrastructure development directly threatens the demand underpinning South Korean exports. Consequently, these chipmakers now face a situation where their growth prospects in the United States may stall or decline due to these new political headwinds.

The impact of this shift is evident when looking at the Bank of Korea data from July regarding shipments in 2025. The United States ranked as the fourth largest destination for South Korean semiconductor exports, with shipments totaling 19.02 billion dollars compared to 13.626 billion dollars three years prior. This growth saw the US share of total exports rise from 9.6 percent to 10.3 percent, while the Chinese mainland remained the largest market. China took shipments worth 74.46 billion dollars in 2025, which represented 40.3 percent of the total semiconductor exports from South Korea. These figures highlight why South Korean firms may now prioritize diversifying their markets toward China to sustain their growth.

The Yonhap News Agency reported in September that South Korea intends to double its semiconductor production capacity within the next five years. To maintain their presence in China, South Korean firms must offer their most advanced products, though US restrictions on high bandwidth memory exports make this difficult. This challenge is compounded by the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which has led to fresh calls in Washington for even tighter restrictions on Chinese chip access. South Korean chipmakers must navigate these pressures while competing against Chinese domestic producers who are making rapid technological progress. These domestic firms possess extensive industrial supply chains that could allow them to scale up production quickly once technical hurdles are overcome.

The Global Times suggests that South Korea should assert its own economic interests because semiconductors are vital to the national economy. The publication argues that chipmakers have every reason to press for more room to sell advanced products in the Chinese market. Following US priorities alone risks undermining South Korean industrial interests, especially as Washington attracts investment while simultaneously imposing restrictive trade barriers. The situation remains complex as memory chip prices stay high, indicating strong underlying demand that South Korean suppliers cannot afford to ignore. Future success will likely depend on whether these firms can overcome American restrictions to serve their largest customer in China.

Articles.Title: GT Voice: AI jitters in US raise stakes in China for S.Korea chip firms - Global Times
